AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_06D53D13.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_06D53D13.statement: The dimensions of a physical quantity are the powers (or exponents) to which the base quantities are raised to represent that quantity.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_4B375DFB.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_4B375DFB.statement: In mechanics, all derived physical quantities can be expressed in terms of the fundamental base dimensions of mass [M], length [L], and time [T].

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_8316E5D4.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_8316E5D4.statement: The dimensions of volume are zero in mass [M^0], 3 in length [L^3], and zero in time [T^0].

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_811EA8BA.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_811EA8BA.statement: The principle of homogeneity of dimensions states that the dimensions of all terms on both sides of a physical equation must be identical.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_62FC21BB.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_62FC21BB.statement: Physical quantities can be added or subtracted if and only if they possess identical dimensions.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_D6365B8F.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_D6365B8F.statement: A physical equation is dimensionally consistent if the dimensions of the left hand side and right hand side are equal.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_2ECFFA8F.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_2ECFFA8F.statement: Dimensional analysis enables conversion of units from one system to another using the invariant relation n1*u1 = n2*u2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_63D40BF8.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_63D40BF8.statement: Dimensional analysis can establish power-law mathematical relationships among physical quantities when their mutual dependencies are known.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_EB371CED.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_EB371CED.statement: Dimensional analysis cannot determine dimensionless proportionality constants.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_866503B1.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_866503B1.statement: Dimensional analysis cannot deduce physical relations involving trigonometric, logarithmic, or exponential functions.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_86358E7D.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_54665F87_86358E7D.statement: Dimensional analysis fails if a physical quantity depends on more variables than the available independent fundamental dimensions.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_DA7F84B0.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_DA7F84B0.statement: Measurement of any physical quantity involves comparison with an internationally accepted reference standard called a unit.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_BABBF96B.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_BABBF96B.statement: The units for fundamental or base quantities are called fundamental or base units.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_C6745CDC.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_C6745CDC.statement: The units of derived physical quantities expressed as combinations of base units are called derived units.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_48859D68.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_48859D68.statement: The International System of Units (SI) is based on seven fundamental base units.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_5C39C275.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_5C39C275.statement: The SI base unit of length is the metre (m) and the SI base unit of mass is the kilogram (kg).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_636A1E20.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_636A1E20.statement: The SI base unit of electric current is the ampere (A) and the thermodynamic temperature is the kelvin (K).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_3B4860F9.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_DEB95734_3B4860F9.statement: Plane angle is measured in radians (rad) and solid angle is measured in steradians (sr) as supplementary SI units.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_5BB4C1F8.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_5BB4C1F8.statement: The uncertainty in the measurement of a physical quantity by any measuring instrument is called error.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_D6FF5DAE.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_D6FF5DAE.statement: Accuracy indicates how close a measured value is to the true value of the physical quantity.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_6B4C0C4F.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_6B4C0C4F.statement: Precision indicates the resolution or limit to which the physical quantity is measured.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_A039AEBD.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_A039AEBD.statement: The smallest value that can be measured by a measuring instrument is called its least count.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_AB6CCE8E.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_AB6CCE8E.statement: Absolute error is the magnitude of the difference between the true value of the quantity and the individual measured value.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_09175661.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_09175661.statement: Relative error is the ratio of the mean absolute error to the mean value of the measured quantity.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_D76BA2D1.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9008E402_D76BA2D1.statement: In multiplication or division, the final result must retain as many significant figures as the measurement with the least significant figures.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_CD4D2C0C.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_CD4D2C0C.statement: A coordinate system along with a clock constitutes a physical frame of reference.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_F8D15ED0.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_F8D15ED0.statement: Path length is the total distance traversed by an object during its motion in a given time interval and is a scalar quantity.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_3FBCF3EC.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_3FBCF3EC.statement: Displacement is the change in position vector of an object in a given time interval and is a vector quantity.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_41439691.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_41439691.statement: Average speed is defined as the total path length divided by the total time interval.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_BAB1AAFF.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_BAB1AAFF.statement: Average velocity is defined as the net displacement divided by the time interval.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_DE97A799.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_057CEE13_DE97A799.statement: The magnitude of displacement is always less than or equal to the total path length traversed.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_CAEE4A04.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_CAEE4A04.statement: Instantaneous velocity is defined as the time derivative of position dx/dt.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_191DEAE6.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_191DEAE6.statement: Instantaneous acceleration is defined as the time derivative of velocity dv/dt.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_494EB9B8.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_494EB9B8.statement: For uniformly accelerated rectilinear motion, final velocity is given by v = v0 + a*t.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_9F55300C.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_9F55300C.statement: For uniformly accelerated rectilinear motion, displacement is given by x - x0 = v0*t + (1/2)*a*t^2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_30B16264.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_30B16264.statement: For uniformly accelerated rectilinear motion, velocity-displacement relation is v^2 = v0^2 + 2*a*(x - x0).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_9A286ACA.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AD1F2FDA_9A286ACA.statement: In free fall under gravity near Earth surface, all bodies experience a constant downward acceleration of magnitude g.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_0861E830.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_0861E830.statement: A scalar quantity is specified completely by a single numerical magnitude and a unit.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_ABA9E76F.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_ABA9E76F.statement: A vector quantity possesses both magnitude and direction and obeys the triangle or parallelogram law of vector addition.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_0DF6D00D.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_0DF6D00D.statement: The magnitude of the resultant of two vectors A and B at angle theta is R = sqrt(A^2 + B^2 + 2*A*B*cos(theta)).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_73C66253.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_73C66253.statement: In two dimensions, a vector A can be resolved into rectangular components Ax = A*cos(theta) and Ay = A*sin(theta).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_A33B7FCC.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_A33B7FCC.statement: The magnitude of a 2D vector with components Ax and Ay is given by |A| = sqrt(Ax^2 + Ay^2).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_A71B7E75.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_4E89B101_A71B7E75.statement: The direction of a 2D vector with components Ax and Ay relative to the x-axis is given by theta = arctan(Ay / Ax).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_C34B2B3B.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_C34B2B3B.statement: Newton First Law of Motion states that a body remains at rest or in uniform straight-line motion unless acted upon by a net external force.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_6F4A7B5E.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_6F4A7B5E.statement: Inertia is the inherent resistance of a body to changes in its state of rest or uniform motion, with mass as its quantitative measure.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_7EDF8194.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_7EDF8194.statement: Linear momentum of a body is defined as the vector product of its mass and velocity: p = m*v.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_7AB71087.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_7AB71087.statement: Newton Second Law states that the applied net external force is equal to the time rate of change of linear momentum: F = dp/dt.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_39C67303.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_39C67303.statement: For constant mass m, Newton second law simplifies to F = m*a.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_47406476.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_0059FC83_47406476.statement: One newton (N) is the force required to produce an acceleration of 1 m/s^2 in a mass of 1 kg.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_8E944C2F.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_8E944C2F.statement: Newton Third Law states that to every action force there is always an equal and opposite reaction force: F_AB = - F_BA.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_CA00FA92.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_CA00FA92.statement: Action and reaction forces act simultaneously on different interacting bodies and never cancel each other.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_B0CFBBFE.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_B0CFBBFE.statement: Impulse is defined as the time integral of force and equals the net change in linear momentum: J = delta p.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_E2F4716A.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_E2F4716A.statement: The total linear momentum of an isolated system with zero net external force is strictly conserved in time.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_12BE6F76.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_12BE6F76.statement: In an isolated two-body collision, initial total momentum equals final total momentum: m1*u1 + m2*u2 = m1*v1 + m2*v2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_BA3ACA98.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_10A164C1_BA3ACA98.statement: The recoil velocity of a gun firing a bullet is given by v_recoil = - (m_bullet / M_gun) * v_bullet.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_C845285E.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_C845285E.statement: Friction is the tangential contact force opposing relative motion or the tendency of relative motion between two contacting surfaces.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_EFCADA71.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_EFCADA71.statement: Static friction is a self-adjusting force whose maximum limiting value is fs_max = mu_s * N.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_0D8F85C4.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_0D8F85C4.statement: Kinetic friction comes into play during relative sliding motion with magnitude fk = mu_k * N.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_F06CFA99.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_F06CFA99.statement: The coefficient of kinetic friction mu_k is generally less than the coefficient of static friction mu_s.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_F0F6523D.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_F0F6523D.statement: Rolling friction is significantly smaller than sliding friction because contact deformation is minimal during rolling.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_3B7C1EB0.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_FCA3AFA8_3B7C1EB0.statement: Methods of reducing friction include lubrication, polishing contact surfaces, and using ball bearings.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_49F23753.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_49F23753.statement: Centripetal acceleration in uniform circular motion is directed radially inward with magnitude a_c = v^2 / R.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_707F0025.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_707F0025.statement: Centripetal force F_c = (m * v^2) / R is the net inward radial force required to maintain circular motion.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_99AAE05A.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_99AAE05A.statement: On a flat level circular road, the maximum speed without skidding is v_max = sqrt(mu_s * R * g).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_EC2AF8F9.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_EC2AF8F9.statement: On a frictionless banked circular road, the optimum safe speed is v_optimum = sqrt(R * g * tan(theta)).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_22CDC09D.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_22CDC09D.statement: On a banked road with friction, the maximum safe speed is v_max = sqrt(R * g * ((mu_s + tan(theta)) / (1 - mu_s * tan(theta)))).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_4B10DF30.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_6202B09B_4B10DF30.statement: Banking of roads directs the horizontal component of the normal reaction inward to provide centripetal force.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_B40F5BD7.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_B40F5BD7.statement: Work done by a constant force F during displacement d is defined as the scalar product W = F . d = F * d * cos(theta).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_EDF9BC49.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_EDF9BC49.statement: Kinetic energy of an object of mass m moving with velocity v is given by K = (1/2) * m * v^2 = p^2 / (2m).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_70EE9783.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_70EE9783.statement: The Work-Energy Theorem states that the work done by the net force on a particle equals the change in its kinetic energy: W_net = Delta K.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_84A1DF1B.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_84A1DF1B.statement: For a variable force F(x), the work done during displacement from initial position to final position is W = Integral F(x) dx.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_C59D7132.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_C59D7132.statement: Work done is positive for acute angles, zero at 90 degrees, and negative for obtuse angles between force and displacement.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_0E021E0D.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_65A072BD_0E021E0D.statement: Kinetic energy of a physical body is always non-negative.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_1E47C4FC.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_1E47C4FC.statement: Potential energy is the stored energy possessed by a body by virtue of its position or configuration.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_A945E79C.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_A945E79C.statement: A force is conservative if the work done by it is independent of the path taken and depends only on initial and final points.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_D1758E57.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_D1758E57.statement: For a conservative force, force is related to potential energy by the spatial derivative F(x) = - dV(x)/dx.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_1A7D8088.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_1A7D8088.statement: The restoring force exerted by an ideal spring stretched or compressed by displacement x is F_s = - k * x.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_A4D4DBDF.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_A4D4DBDF.statement: The potential energy stored in an ideal spring of spring constant k at displacement x is V_s = (1/2) * k * x^2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_BEE213A5.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_017FC3AC_BEE213A5.statement: The total mechanical energy of an isolated system remains constant under conservative forces: Delta E = 0.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_670AC602.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_670AC602.statement: Power is defined as the time rate of doing work or transferring energy: P = dW/dt = F . v.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_1F4ED078.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_1F4ED078.statement: The SI unit of power is the watt (W = J/s), where 1 horsepower equals 746 watts.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_AE20ED79.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_AE20ED79.statement: In all physical collisions, total linear momentum is strictly conserved because external forces are negligible during collision.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_C717A04D.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_C717A04D.statement: In an elastic collision, both total linear momentum and total kinetic energy are conserved with coefficient of restitution e = 1.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_66B655EC.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_66B655EC.statement: In an inelastic collision, total linear momentum is conserved while total kinetic energy is not conserved, with 0 <= e < 1.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_4F62FAAD.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_87EB50DB_4F62FAAD.statement: In a completely inelastic collision, the interacting bodies stick together after impact and move with common final velocity.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_84AFE37F.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_84AFE37F.statement: The centre of mass of a system of particles is the unique point where the entire mass of the system may be considered concentrated.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_C395E73D.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_C395E73D.statement: For a two-particle system with masses m1 and m2 at r1 and r2, the centre of mass position vector is R_cm = (m1*r1 + m2*r2) / (m1 + m2).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_FBCC716C.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_FBCC716C.statement: For an n-particle system, the position vector of the centre of mass is R_cm = (1/M) * Sum(m_i * r_i).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_88553E96.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_88553E96.statement: For a continuous mass distribution with total mass M, the centre of mass is given by R_cm = (1/M) * Integral(r dm).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_33020B8F.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_33020B8F.statement: For symmetrical bodies of uniform density, the centre of mass coincides with their geometric centre.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_48E93743.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_7E2B0101_48E93743.statement: The centre of mass of a body does not necessarily lie inside the material of the body.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_16797F82.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_16797F82.topic: Linear Momentum of System of Particles
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_16797F82.statement: The total linear momentum of a system of particles is equal to the product of total mass M and the velocity of its centre of mass: P_total = M * V_cm.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_36235CB2.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_36235CB2.topic: Linear Momentum of System of Particles
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_36235CB2.statement: The motion of the centre of mass of a system of particles is governed exclusively by net external force: M * A_cm = F_ext.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_1F434645.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_1F434645.topic: Linear Momentum of System of Particles
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_1F434645.statement: The sum of all internal forces between constituent particles of an isolated system is zero by Newton's third law.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_AA4E5D9A.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_AA4E5D9A.topic: Linear Momentum of System of Particles
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_AA4E5D9A.statement: If net external force acting on a system is zero, the velocity of the centre of mass remains constant and total linear momentum is conserved.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_3917E7D0.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_3917E7D0.topic: Linear Momentum of System of Particles
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_3917E7D0.statement: Internal forces can alter the relative velocities of constituent particles but cannot alter the motion of the centre of mass.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_2832C46C.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_2832C46C.topic: Linear Momentum of System of Particles
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_9A3C0201_2832C46C.statement: The velocity of the centre of mass is given by V_cm = dR_cm/dt = (1/M) * Sum(m_i * v_i).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_456D0DFA.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_456D0DFA.topic: Center of Mass of Rigid Body
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_456D0DFA.statement: A rigid body is a body with a perfectly fixed shape where relative distances between all constituent particles remain constant.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_FFDB45E4.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_FFDB45E4.topic: Center of Mass of Rigid Body
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_FFDB45E4.statement: General motion of a rigid body can be decomposed into translation of its centre of mass and rotation about the centre of mass.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_44B4DE37.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_44B4DE37.topic: Center of Mass of Rigid Body
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_44B4DE37.statement: In pure translational motion, all particles of a rigid body have identical velocities and accelerations at any given instant.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_C413FC5D.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_C413FC5D.topic: Center of Mass of Rigid Body
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_C413FC5D.statement: In pure rotational motion about a fixed axis, all particles move in circles with the same angular velocity omega.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_8FE14689.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_8FE14689.topic: Center of Mass of Rigid Body
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_8B5D7BD6_8FE14689.statement: If a projectile explodes in mid-air, the centre of mass of its fragments continues along the original parabolic trajectory under gravity.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_D6A5D0AE.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_D6A5D0AE.statement: The vector product of two vectors A and B is C = A x B = |A| * |B| * sin(theta) * n_hat and is anti-commutative: A x B = - (B x A).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_F4B687A5.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_F4B687A5.statement: Torque tau of a force F acting at position vector r with respect to an origin is defined as tau = r x F.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_1AC170B4.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_1AC170B4.statement: Angular momentum L of a particle with position vector r and linear momentum p is defined as L = r x p.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_36EF74D9.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_36EF74D9.statement: The time rate of change of angular momentum of a particle or system equals the applied net external torque: dL/dt = tau_ext.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_D2460AED.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_D2460AED.statement: The Law of Conservation of Angular Momentum states that if total external torque is zero, total angular momentum remains constant.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_92D0A89C.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_AB220534_92D0A89C.statement: The magnitude of torque is |tau| = r * F * sin(theta) = F * r_perp, with SI unit newton-metre (N*m).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_4DA53D85.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_4DA53D85.statement: A rigid body is in mechanical equilibrium if and only if both translational equilibrium and rotational equilibrium are satisfied simultaneously.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_37A5FDCC.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_37A5FDCC.statement: The Principle of Moments for a lever in rotational equilibrium states that load times load arm equals effort times effort arm.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_2C707B98.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_2C707B98.statement: For rotational motion with constant angular acceleration alpha, final angular velocity is given by omega = omega0 + alpha * t.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_084A1FCF.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_084A1FCF.statement: For rotational motion with constant angular acceleration alpha, angular displacement is given by theta = omega0 * t + (1/2) * alpha * t^2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_219CBAC8.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_219CBAC8.statement: For rotational motion with constant angular acceleration alpha, the velocity-displacement relation is omega^2 = omega0^2 + 2 * alpha * theta.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_C91AE3F9.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1367A8D3_C91AE3F9.statement: Mechanical advantage of a lever is the ratio of load force to effort force: MA = F_load / F_effort = d_effort / d_load.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_8CAE2DC0.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_8CAE2DC0.statement: Moment of inertia (I) is the rotational analogue of mass measuring resistance to rotational acceleration: I = Sum(m_i * r_i^2).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_21EC7CBE.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_21EC7CBE.statement: The radius of gyration (k) of a body is the distance from the axis of rotation where the entire mass M could be placed: I = M * k^2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_647D8984.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_647D8984.statement: The moment of inertia of a uniform circular ring of mass M and radius R about its central perpendicular axis is I = M * R^2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_7EA0F8A3.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_7EA0F8A3.statement: The moment of inertia of a uniform circular disc of mass M and radius R about its central perpendicular axis is I = (1/2) * M * R^2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_2C06A2B4.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_2C06A2B4.statement: The moment of inertia of a uniform solid sphere of mass M and radius R about its diameter is I = (2/5) * M * R^2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_A8BB6369.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_A8BB6369.statement: The Parallel Axis Theorem states that I = I_cm + M * d^2, where d is the perpendicular distance between the parallel axes.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_D7D82CF3.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_2218270C_D7D82CF3.statement: The Perpendicular Axis Theorem for planar laminar bodies states that I_z = I_x + I_y.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_DBC7CBFB.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_DBC7CBFB.statement: Rotational kinetic energy of a body with moment of inertia I rotating with angular velocity omega is K_rot = (1/2) * I * omega^2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_CCBB04EE.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_CCBB04EE.statement: The total kinetic energy of a body rolling without slipping with linear speed v_cm is K_total = (1/2) * M * v_cm^2 * [1 + k^2 / R^2].

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_1AE53CFF.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_1AE53CFF.statement: The linear acceleration of a body rolling down an incline of angle theta without slipping is a_cm = (g * sin(theta)) / [1 + k^2 / R^2].

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_D3B00BF4.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_D3B00BF4.statement: For a body rolling without slipping on a horizontal surface, the linear velocity of the centre of mass is v_cm = R * omega.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_9A4AB3E4.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_9A4AB3E4.statement: A solid sphere reaches the bottom of an inclined plane before a cylinder or ring because its k^2/R^2 value is the lowest.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_DB367E6F.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_1C4E0301_DB367E6F.statement: In pure rolling motion without slipping, the instantaneous velocity of the point of contact with the ground is zero.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_3D48D86E_9DE21698.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_3D48D86E_9DE21698.statement: Kepler's First Law (Law of Orbits) states that all planets move in elliptical orbits with the Sun situated at one focus.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_3D48D86E_D9FC3B34.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_3D48D86E_D9FC3B34.statement: Kepler's Second Law (Law of Areas) states that the areal velocity of a planet revolving around the Sun is constant: dA/dt = L / (2m) = constant.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_3D48D86E_2CD2F7CD.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_3D48D86E_2CD2F7CD.statement: Kepler's Second Law is a direct mathematical consequence of the conservation of angular momentum under a central gravitational force.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_3D48D86E_4EE99DEA.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_3D48D86E_4EE99DEA.statement: Kepler's Third Law (Law of Periods) states that the square of the orbital period T of a planet is proportional to the cube of the semi-major axis a.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_3D48D86E_80F5B79F.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_3D48D86E_80F5B79F.statement: A revolving planet moves with maximum speed at perihelion and minimum speed at aphelion.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_5C60A7A0.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_5C60A7A0.statement: Newton's Universal Law of Gravitation states that the attractive force between two masses is F = G * (m1 * m2) / r^2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_BFD5EC35.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_BFD5EC35.statement: The Universal Gravitational Constant G has the value 6.674 x 10^-11 N*m^2 / kg^2 with dimensions [M^-1 L^3 T^-2].

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_18E24EE1.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_18E24EE1.statement: Gravitational force between two particles is an attractive central force that acts along the line joining their centres.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_F16CA48C.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_F16CA48C.statement: The Principle of Superposition states that the net gravitational force on a particle is the vector sum of individual forces from all other particles.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_BE4CD636.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_BE4CD636.statement: The gravitational constant G is independent of the intervening medium, temperature, and nature of the interacting bodies.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_026B2A1F.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_BACFBE4A_026B2A1F.statement: Gravitational force forms an action-reaction pair obeying Newton's third law: F_12 = - F_21.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_EFC26508.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_EFC26508.statement: The acceleration due to gravity at Earth's surface of mass M_e and radius R_e is g = G * M_e / R_e^2.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_0E987CEF.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_0E987CEF.statement: At height h above Earth's surface, acceleration due to gravity decreases according to g(h) = g * [1 - 2*h/R_e].

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_5ED99053.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_5ED99053.statement: At depth d below Earth's surface, acceleration due to gravity decreases linearly according to g(d) = g * [1 - d/R_e].

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_5A4C9B7F.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_5A4C9B7F.statement: The acceleration due to gravity is maximum at Earth's surface and becomes exactly zero at the centre of the Earth.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_A4B953D2.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_A4B953D2.statement: Due to Earth's rotation, effective acceleration due to gravity at latitude lambda is g_eff = g - omega^2 * R_e * cos^2(lambda).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_B0349097.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_5F4143EE_B0349097.statement: Acceleration due to gravity on Earth is maximum at the poles and minimum at the equator.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_F2BA44A7.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_F2BA44A7.statement: Gravitational potential energy of two point masses m1 and m2 separated by distance r is U(r) = - G * (m1 * m2) / r.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_E74E7270.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_E74E7270.statement: Gravitational potential V at distance r from mass M is the potential energy per unit mass: V(r) = - G * M / r.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_30720FDC.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_30720FDC.statement: Gravitational potential energy U(r) is always negative for finite separation with zero reference at infinite separation.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_C8D8F6A8.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_C8D8F6A8.statement: The relationship between gravitational field intensity E_g and gravitational potential V is E_g = - dV/dr.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_0A0E33A4.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_0A0E33A4.statement: Near Earth's surface, the change in gravitational potential energy for height h is Delta U = m * g * h.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_A969A111.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_B821705D_A969A111.statement: Gravitational potential is a scalar quantity with SI unit joules per kilogram (J/kg).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_1AE96603.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_1AE96603.statement: Escape speed from Earth surface is the minimum projection speed to escape gravitational pull: v_e = sqrt(2 * G * M_e / R_e) = sqrt(2 * g * R_e).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_0A9E45D9.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_0A9E45D9.statement: The numerical value of escape speed from Earth's surface is approximately 11.2 km/s and is independent of projectile mass and projection angle.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_6B26DE21.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_6B26DE21.statement: The orbital speed of a satellite orbiting Earth at radius r is v_o = sqrt(G * M_e / r).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_F6AB3F2B.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_F6AB3F2B.statement: For a satellite in close Earth orbit, orbital speed is v_o = sqrt(g * R_e) ~= 7.92 km/s, and v_e = sqrt(2) * v_o.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_73AE0DD0.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_73AE0DD0.statement: The orbital time period of a satellite is T = 2*pi * sqrt(r^3 / (G * M_e)).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_FBDEF4F5.subject: Physics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_PHY_A8EBEA76_FBDEF4F5.statement: The total mechanical energy of an orbiting satellite is negative: E = - (1/2) * G * M_e * m / r, proving it is in a bound orbit.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_37A79A64.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_37A79A64.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_37A79A64.statement: The Law of Conservation of Mass states that matter can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_D8263123.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_D8263123.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_D8263123.statement: The Law of Definite Proportions states that a given chemical compound always contains exactly the same proportion of elements by mass.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_35B08AE8.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_35B08AE8.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_35B08AE8.statement: The Law of Multiple Proportions states that if two elements combine to form more than one compound, the masses of one element that combine with a fixed mass of the other are in the ratio of small whole numbers.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_F7989E2A.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_F7989E2A.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_F7989E2A.statement: Gay-Lussac's Law states that when gases combine or are produced in a chemical reaction, they do so in a simple ratio by volume, provided all gases are at the same temperature and pressure.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_00838222.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_00838222.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_00838222.statement: Avogadro's Law states that equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal number of molecules.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_60CCB0AC.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_60CCB0AC.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_60CCB0AC.statement: Dalton's Atomic Theory postulates that matter consists of indivisible atoms, and all atoms of a given element have identical mass and chemical properties.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_A6FB4DD1.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_A6FB4DD1.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_A6FB4DD1.statement: One atomic mass unit (1 u) is defined as a mass exactly equal to one-twelfth of the mass of one carbon-12 atom: 1 u = 1.66056 x 10^-24 g.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_0B9BC18A.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_0B9BC18A.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_0B9BC18A.statement: One mole is the amount of substance that contains exactly 6.02214076 x 10^23 elementary entities, known as the Avogadro constant (N_A).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_2D5B52FE.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_2D5B52FE.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_2D5B52FE.statement: The mass of one mole of a substance in grams is called its molar mass (M), which is numerically equal to its atomic or molecular mass in unified mass units (g/mol).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_F2268E36.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_F2268E36.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_F2268E36.statement: In the combustion of methane CH4(g) + 2 O2(g) -> CO2(g) + 2 H2O(g), 1 mole of CH4 reacts with 2 moles of O2 to produce 1 mole of CO2 and 2 moles of H2O.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_0545534C.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_0545534C.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_0545534C.statement: The limiting reagent is the reactant that is completely consumed first in a chemical reaction and limits the amount of product formed.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_C8E94EA8.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_C8E94EA8.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_C8E94EA8.statement: Molarity (M) is defined as the number of moles of solute dissolved in one litre of solution: M = (moles of solute) / (volume of solution in litres).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_FBE5DD02.subject: Chemistry
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_FBE5DD02.topic: Matter, Dalton's Atomic Theory, Laws of Chemical Combination, Atomic and Molecular Masses, Mole Concept
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_CHE_910B0B49_FBE5DD02.statement: Molality (m) is defined as the number of moles of solute present in 1 kg of solvent and is temperature-independent because mass does not change with temperature.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_D1B6F61D.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_D1B6F61D.statement: A set is a well-defined collection of distinct objects.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_8E8CCB25.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_8E8CCB25.statement: If an object a is an element of set A, it is written as a ∈ A; if b is not an element of set A, it is written as b ∉ A.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_621F66AA.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_621F66AA.statement: Standard number sets are denoted as N for natural numbers, Z for integers, Q = {p/q : p, q ∈ Z and q ≠ 0} for rational numbers, and R for real numbers.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_D3AE90CF.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_D3AE90CF.statement: In roster or tabular form, all elements of a set are listed separated by commas within braces {}, where listing order is immaterial and elements are not repeated.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_6FF4E366.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_6FF4E366.statement: In set-builder form, a set is represented by stating the single characterizing property shared by all its elements: A = {x : P(x)}.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_E7B2ED50.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_E7B2ED50.statement: The empty set (or null/void set) contains no elements, is denoted by ϕ or {}, and has cardinality n(ϕ) = 0.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_2E310406.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_2E310406.statement: A set is finite if it is empty or consists of a definite number of distinct elements n(A); otherwise, it is an infinite set.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_87E2CF75.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_87E2CF75.statement: Two sets A and B are equal (A = B) if they have identical elements, whereas sets with equal cardinality n(A) = n(B) are equivalent sets.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_8092F0EE.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_8092F0EE.statement: A set A is a subset of B (A ⊆ B) if every element of A is also an element of B (a ∈ A => a ∈ B); if A ⊆ B and A ≠ B, then A is a proper subset (A ⊂ B).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_CC297DF5.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_CC297DF5.statement: Every set is a subset of itself (A ⊆ A), and the empty set is a subset of every set (ϕ ⊆ A).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_871D5B7E.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_871D5B7E.statement: Two sets A and B are equal (A = B) if and only if A ⊆ B and B ⊆ A.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_79B21169.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_79B21169.statement: Open interval (a, b) = {x ∈ R : a < x < b} excludes endpoints, whereas closed interval [a, b] = {x ∈ R : a <= x <= b} includes both endpoints.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_9C2209FD.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_9C2209FD.statement: Semi-open intervals are [a, b) = {x ∈ R : a <= x < b} and (a, b] = {x ∈ R : a < x <= b}, and the length of each interval is (b - a).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_69C8729D.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_69C8729D.statement: The power set P(A) is the collection of all subsets of set A, where both ϕ ∈ P(A) and A ∈ P(A).

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_39AE4B48.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_39AE4B48.statement: If a finite set A has n(A) = m elements, the power set has cardinality n(P(A)) = 2^m, and the number of proper subsets is 2^m - 1.

AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_72B3D5FA.subject: Mathematics
AF_GU_JEEMAIN2027_MAT_9BB8FB46_72B3D5FA.statement: A universal set U is a comprehensive superset containing all objects, elements, and sets under consideration in a given mathematical context.
